source.title: Memory and the Sense of Personal Identity

confidence_rationale: This is the sharpest available attack on the specific inferential step MECH-079 makes, and it converges independently on the R7 disposition already recorded against the claim. Klein and Nichols report patient R.B., who during a defined period retrieved accurate, specific, one-of-a-kind autobiographical episodes -- correct content, correctly indexed to himself rather than to another person -- while lacking the first-personal sense that 'I had these experiences'. Content was intact; mineness was absent. If retrieved content and its correct self-indexing can be fully present while phenomenal ownership is absent, then no mechanism that delivers content and indexing -- which is all stable map geometry could deliver -- is sufficient for the phenomenal continuity MECH-079 says it produces. The claim's chain has a missing final link, and this is a positive demonstration of the gap rather than an argument from absence. Held at 0.71 because it is a single case in a philosophy journal, the mineness deficit is established by patient report against which there is no independent instrument, and the inference from 'insufficient' to 'not the mechanism' is mine rather than the authors'.
failure_signatures: A single patient's introspective report is the sole instrument for the presence or absence of mineness. There is no third-person measure, so the dissociation is exactly as strong as the report, and a sceptic may hold that R.B. lost a metacognitive judgement about his memories rather than their phenomenal ownership. Nothing in the case adjudicates between those two readings.

The case establishes that content plus correct self-indexing is INSUFFICIENT for phenomenal ownership. It does not establish that map geometry is irrelevant to ownership, and it is fully compatible with map geometry being necessary-but-not-sufficient. Citing this entry as showing that selfhood is independent of hippocampal geometry would over-read it.

Klein and Nichols draw a conclusion about memory-based accounts of personal identity in the philosophical sense; they make no claim about hippocampal map geometry and do not report imaging or lesion localisation for R.B. The substrate link that would connect their dissociation to MECH-079's mechanism is supplied by REE, not by the source.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Patient R.B. was able, during a defined period, to retrieve highly specific autobiographical episodes with accurate content, and to represent that those episodes were about himself rather than another person, while lacking the first-personal sense that 'I had these experiences' -- the autonoetic sense of ownership or mineness. Klein and Nichols conclude that the sense of personal identity decomposes into two separable components, one supplying memory content and another generating the sense of mineness, and that mineness is therefore a contingent rather than constitutive feature of remembering.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-079's chain runs same topology -> similar rollouts -> similar commitments -> subjective identity persistence. Everything up to 'similar commitments' is content and indexing: what is retrieved, and that it is retrieved as mine-labelled. R.B. shows that a system can have all of that and still lack the phenomenal ownership the final arrow asserts. For REE this means that even a perfect implementation of stable anchor geometry, reproducible rollouts and persistent context-conditioned commitments would establish only the operational leg -- persistence of choices and of retrieved autobiographical associations -- and would leave the phenomenal leg untouched, because the biological case shows those two come apart in the direction that matters. This is independent convergence on the claim's existing R7 audit disposition: phenomenological continuity is conflated with choice persistence.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a single case, and the absence of mineness rests entirely on R.B.'s own report with no independent instrument -- which is the same measurement problem MECH-079 has in V3, arriving from the other side. The case shows content-plus-indexing is INSUFFICIENT for phenomenal ownership; it does not show map geometry is irrelevant, and it is compatible with geometry being necessary but not sufficient. The authors themselves argue about memory-based theories of personal identity and never mention hippocampal geometry; the bridge to MECH-079's substrate is REE's, and it should be cited as such.
mapping.source_context: Single neurological case report embedded in a philosophical argument; human, self-report and clinical interview, no imaging or lesion localisation reported for the dissociation.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality 0.62: Mind is a leading philosophy journal and the case is carefully argued, but the evidential base is one patient and one uncorroborated introspective report, which is weak by empirical standards even where it is decisive by conceptual ones. Mapping fidelity 0.85 -- unusually high, because the dissociation is between exactly the two things MECH-079 runs together, so the source speaks to the claim's actual inferential structure rather than to an adjacent mechanism. Transfer risk 0.35, low for this corpus: the transfer is human-to-REE at the level of an argument about sufficiency, not an animal-to-human extrapolation of a measured effect.
